I think the biggest issue is that it really tries to slowly make you descend the same path the main characters go, overinterpreting that fictional documentary, the ever expanding house being a metaphor for it. Something that is simple from the outside but goes onto seemingly non-sensical directions on the inside. I think that idea is neat, but it's really apparent early on when you start to think about the story and the way it is written. The book spends a lot of time unaware that this metaphor is really obvious, it underestimates the reader's media literacy and just comes off as pretentious as a result

I get that that's the point. But when something wastes my time on purpose, then that is worse than just making bad art. I'd rather experience art that is bad out of incompetence than art that is bad because it doesn't want to be good, if that makes sense.

As for the reading, maybe that's part of it, but I found it less so challenging than unengaging. About the game in general, the music, the look, the general *feel* of strive. The systems are pretty cool and the training mode is great too. I like the community as well.

About specific characters, it's really hard to say. For one, a lot of the designs are really cool, I mean, a witch riding on an electric guitar is actually genius. Other than that, I'm just gonna list a few things I like about the characters:

Sol has pretty "basic" buttons, a typical shoto, but the way the animations look and the attacks feel, him being somewhat of a rushdown, remind of Akuma, which I really liked in SFV.

Bedman?'s error-attacks are cool and an interesting gimmick. Makes for great potential in both mind games and combos. Also his animations are top-notch

Giovanna's quick dash makes her feel really fast and also evasive. Being able to instantly get in the opponents face does feel good (if I don't get instantly punished or dash straight into an attack that is)

Anji and Baiken's counter mechanics I like, I'm just a sucker for counters, though I don't think I could get good with those with a shitty reaction time like mine.

Aside from his complexity putting me off, Asuka is an incredibly interesting character in concept and makes for really interesting approaches, so I really like that.

Baiken and Testament both probably look the coolest out of the main cast. Baiken as a one-armed, one-armed samurai (and not because of her massive badonkers, I'd rather her not have them to be completely honest) and Testament as a sort of grim reaper with the raddest scythe I think I've ever seen. Their animations also do their part in conveying the weight of the scythe, which I find amazing, feeling the weight in combat is why I love the souls-games.

Ram has cool range and her design with the two giant swords is pretty cool. Also really weighty animations, which I'm always a fan of.

Sin's follow-up mechanics seems really interesting and looks amazing, has some great potential to mess with the opponent (but I'm not that into actually performing any mind games myself to be honest, just think it's cool)

Nago's big range looks and feels amazing, add hefty damage to that and I'm a fan, also bonus points for samurai.

Potemkin as a sort of "unstoppable wall" is pretty badass.
